title: Object hero: the product is the page
summary: One featured product, shot like a specimen, with the buy control fixed to the object. Use for single-item launches.

layout.skeleton: 7/5 split; the product image sits left, offset 1 column, and overlaps into a facts band
layout.focus: the featured product, with its price and one provenance fact beside it
layout.desktop: product name as a 72px display line over the image edge; brief facts (size, notes, date) as a 3-line ledger
layout.mobile: product full-width at 62vh, ledger below, sticky add bar
layout.rhythm: 96px between bands; the ledger uses a 24px baseline

imagery.subject: the product on a plain surface with a few raw-material props
imagery.crop: tight, with the product cut by the right edge
imagery.fallback: a CSS label block: product name in ink on a material-tone panel

motion.effect: bag count ticks and the pill settles 4px

action.instruction: One primary action attached to the product. Fill it from the brief's product, size and price, and never repeat it in a hero band
action.label: Add [product], [size] — [price]

why: A first-time buyer needs one choice, not a catalogue. Making the object the hero and stating the brief's exact facts reads warm and exact.

sources.observation: Agrumea Farm hero: the product jars are the hero on cream paper with an oxblood shape and type set on a curve; the only CTA is a small pill on the featured jar ('Scopri il prodotto').

credit: Agrumea Farm site (Awwwards submission; designer not verified)

title: Exception first: the problem owns the screen
summary: The most urgent item is promoted out of the list into a full-width strip, with its position in the queue; every other row stays quiet. Use for time-pressured operations queues.

layout.skeleton: exception strip on top (item ID, location, deviation), the full queue table below, a due-next rail on the right
layout.focus: the deviation value at 40px tabular figures, with an 'n / total' position label
layout.desktop: 12-col; strip spans 12, table 8, rail 4 holding the next item due
layout.mobile: strip, then rail, then table as stacked rows

imagery.subject: none; location codes act as the visuals
imagery.fallback: location code set at 24px tabular figures

motion.effect: the value cross-fades; the strip edge pulses once

action.instruction: Focus jumps the table filter to the exception. Fill it from the brief's most urgent item
action.label: Focus [item ID] at [location]

why: An operator on the clock should see the one problem before the list. Calm comes from making everything except the exception quiet.

sources.observation: Linear's home page product mock (server HTML) shows one focused issue 'DRV-8852' with a '1 / 84' queue position, a sidebar of 'Inbox | My issues | Reviews', and a properties rail ('In Progress | Medium | Karri'): one item in focus, its place in the queue, and its state beside it.

credit: Linear (Linear Orbit), home page product mock

title: Platform sign: departure as signage
summary: Time and place set like a station sign; the credential opens in one tap. Use for on-the-move transit, tickets or boarding.

layout.skeleton: sign block (time, destination, platform) on an ink band, then the credential reveal, then alternatives and pass options
layout.focus: departure time at 60px plus a platform badge
layout.desktop: centered 420px column; the rest of the page is empty paper
layout.mobile: sign band fills the top 40%; reveal button in the thumb zone

motion.effect: the credential slides up from the sign band to show the code

action.instruction: The button names the credential from the brief, not 'View'
action.label: Show ticket [ticket ID]

why: A walking rider reads at a glance. Signage-scale numerals and a single reveal beat card-stacked layouts for speed.

sources.observation: GOV.UK: 'Write button text in sentence case, describing the action it performs.'
.typography-body is 17px at -0.022em, a readable body floor.

title: Ground plane: full-bleed built work
summary: The lead project opens as a full-bleed site photograph under a serif title; the other projects sit small and off the grid. Use for spatial practices.

layout.skeleton: full-bleed lead project; title split across two lines; secondary projects offset at 1/3 width; contact in a quiet footer
layout.focus: lead project title at 120px, with its scale and completion year from the brief
layout.desktop: Title bottom-left on an opaque paper panel overlapping the image edge. Facts align in a right-hand column.
layout.mobile: image at 70vh; title below it, not overlaid
layout.rhythm: 160px section gaps; empty space as the material

imagery.subject: the built site at ground or eye level, with planting or material in the foreground
imagery.fallback: site-plan line drawing in ink on paper

motion.effect: the image scales 1.04 to 1 (the one signature move)

action.instruction: Primary link opens the lead case study; contact is plain text
action.label: Open the [project] case study

why: Spacious and material: built work needs room. A serif display paired with a quiet sans and a full-bleed ground reads as real work, not a template.

sources.observation: Studio Dado (viewed): the serif display 'FORM FOLLOWS FEELING' is set full-bleed over warm material photography, with a small sans nav on an offset grid.
Studio D live HTML: 'Spatial design at eye level', positioning spatial practice in plain words.

title: Scale ledger: plans as stops on one quantity
summary: Plans are compared along the single quantity buyers pay for, not shown as identical cards. Use when tiers differ mainly by an amount.

layout.skeleton: a horizontal bar from 0 to the largest tier's quantity, with each plan as a stop; feature differences listed under each stop
layout.focus: the recommended middle stop, labelled with its quantity and key feature
layout.desktop: bar spans 10 cols, with stops placed proportionally; prices sit above the stops
layout.mobile: bar turns vertical; stops become rows
layout.rhythm: 12px base; 48px between the bar and the details

imagery.subject: none; the bar is the image

motion.effect: the fill moves to the stop

action.instruction: Continue with the chosen plan, naming the plan and price from the brief
action.label: Continue with [plan] — [price]/[period]

why: Buyers pay for a quantity. One proportional scale makes the choice legible, and naming the plan and price on the button is assured, not loud.

sources.observation: GOV.UK: button text should describe 'the action it performs'.

title: Margin front: feature at reading width
summary: The lead story runs at reading width with an italic deck; secondary items run in a narrow margin column. Use for small editorial homes.

layout.skeleton: feature title across 8 cols, standfirst at 62ch; a 3-col margin column holds the secondary dispatch and a recipe card
layout.focus: feature title, with byline and read time from the brief
layout.desktop: asymmetric 8/1/3 split; the title breaks into the margin
layout.mobile: feature first, then dispatch, then recipe

imagery.subject: the feature's setting or material, top-down
imagery.fallback: an ink rule plus a large italic drop numeral of the read time

motion.trigger: Open the feature by tap or keyboard
motion.effect: Reveal the standfirst and underline the active link as the reading view opens
motion.reduced: Open the reading view immediately and preserve focus

action.instruction: Headline and button both open the feature
action.label: Read [feature title]

why: Tactile, observant reading wants a comfortable measure and print logic: rules, margins and an italic voice instead of card grids.

sources.observation: Butterick: 'Aim for an average line length of 45–90 characters, including spaces.'
